_comment: API key configurations for service-to-service authentication. Create keys via: op auth api-keys create --config configs/api-keys.json

keys.name: ETL Pipeline Service
keys.description: API key for the nightly ETL pipeline that ingests data from the data warehouse. Scoped to data and pipeline operations only.

keys.name: CI/CD Deployment Service
keys.description: API key for the CI/CD pipeline that deploys applications and plugins. Scoped to app deployment and plugin management.

keys.name: Monitoring Dashboard Reader
keys.description: Read-only API key for the Grafana monitoring dashboard. Queries execution logs and pipeline status for observability panels.

keys.name: Audit Export Service
keys.description: API key for exporting audit logs to the enterprise SIEM (Splunk). Scoped to audit and log read/export only.

keys.name: Partner Integration (Globex)
keys.description: API key for the Globex partner integration. Limited to reading shared datasets. Tenant-scoped to the Globex tenant.

keyFormat._comment: Reference documentation for API key format. Not processed by the CLI.

bestPractices._comment: Security guidelines for API key management. Not processed by the CLI.
rules: Never embed API keys in source code or commit them to version control.
Store API keys in a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, etc.).
Use the minimum required scopes for each key (principle of least privilege).
Set an expiration date on every key. Prefer shorter lifetimes.
Rotate keys regularly. Use the autoRotate policy for automated rotation.
Revoke keys immediately when a service is decommissioned.
Monitor the lastUsedAt field to detect unused keys for cleanup.
A user cannot create an API key with scopes they do not possess.
